newsitem.title: UK: UK set for EU showdown over working week -- paper.
newsitem.headline: UK set for EU showdown over working week -- paper.

text.p: The British government is set to trigger another major showdown with European Union partners if a European Court of Justice decision, due in 10 days, imposes a maximum 48-hour working week across Europe, the Financial Times said on Friday.

The FT said the British government, which has fiercely resisted the move as restrictive to business, will threaten to veto EU reforms proposed at the intergovernmental conference if the 48-hour week maximum is imposed.
One unnamed minister was quoted in the report as saying that the EU would "have to play ball" when facing a threat to the new European treaty under negotiation.
"We really don't care whether or not there is a new treaty," he said.

The decision to take a hardline stance against the possible limit on working hours was taken by the British cabinet, after receiving legal advice that it would be difficult to delay implementation of the ruling, the paper said.
The deadline for bringing in the maximum 48-hour working week is reported to be November 23 across all EU states.

The report added that the Prime Minister John Major personally felt very strongly about the issue and was not prepared to surrender after securing the opt-out clause from Europe's Social Chapter, which covers working conditions.
The FT said that Major is understood to be willing to campaign on the issue in the upcoming general election unless the working rule is "disapplied" in Britain.
